_extraction_flags.notes: Valid Simulation/Analytic Paper. Focuses on Adaptive Resource Allocation for ADO-OFDM in OW-ISAC.

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Fig 1: ADO-OFDM OW-ISAC system model. Fig 2: Power allocation curves. Fig 3/4: Pareto Fronts (Trade-off curves) between Spectral Efficiency (Comm) and Fisher Information/Sensing Precision.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: OW-ISAC (LiDAR + OWC). Waveform: ADO-OFDM (Asymmetrically Clipped DC Biased Optical OFDM). Hybrid of DCO-OFDM and ACO-OFDM. Problem: Joint Resource Allocation (DCO/ACO Power Split + Subcarrier Power Allocation).
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Sensing Precision (CRLB based) vs Comm Spectral Efficiency trade-off. Shows DCO-OFDM dominance in Comm-centric and ACO-OFDM utility in Sensing-centric regimes (at low frequencies).
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: ADO-OFDM allows flexibility. Optimization problem decomposed into DCO-ACO split and Subcarrier allocation. Weighted-sum objective balances C&S.

application.scenario_description: OW-ISAC transceiver on a LiDAR estimating distance to OWC receiver while communicating.

key_contribution.key_contribution: Adaptive Resource Allocation (Power & Subcarriers) for ADO-OFDM based OW-ISAC. Decomposes non-convex joint optimization into DCO-ACO power distribution and convex subcarrier allocation sub-problems.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: Lack of adaptive resource allocation schemes for ADO-OFDM in OW-ISAC to balance communication spectral efficiency and sensing Fisher information.

transmitter.notes: ADO-OFDM: DCO-OFDM (Even subcarriers) + ACO-OFDM (Odd subcarriers). N=1024.

waveform.notes: Unified ADO-OFDM waveform. Sensing via Pilots/Data (Frequency Domain Channel Estimation for ToF).

comm_metrics.notes: Metric is Spectral Efficiency (bps/Hz). Optimization target.

sensing_metrics.notes: Metric is Fisher Information (proxy for CRB/Precision). ~2cm resolution observed in figures.

tradeoff.notes: Pareto front shown for Spectral Efficiency vs Ranging Precision. Weight factor rho controls the trade-off.
